method: Saved log and source inspection only. No builds, tests, replay, browser sessions or benchmarks launched.
rootCause: Not established. The evidence cannot distinguish a driver/kernel/hardware stall, blocked I/O, or a transient event missed by sampling.
observations: The interrupted 64-cubed active ice-heat replay did not create a gameplay renderer. Its last progress is tick 464, reported only every 16 ticks; the failing tick and operation are unknown.
Supervisor and progress records cease about 37 seconds after launch. No exit code, timeout or completed receipt was recorded.

Event 41 records an unclean restart at 18:54:52 PDT with BugcheckCode 0 and WHEABootErrorCount 0. This does not identify the cause. Event 6008's estimated shutdown precedes valid run logs and is not used as the freeze time.
The sampled maxima do not show sustained CPU saturation, GPU overheating or memory exhaustion. They cannot exclude unsampled spikes, CPU thermals, power or driver faults.
Free GPU memory fell about 2.3 GiB during the interrupted run. Allocation ownership was not recorded; attribution to another application or the harness is unsupported.
An earlier CPU overload was stopped cleanly. A successful comparable replay had a larger recorded monitor lag than the interrupted replay. Neither metric identifies a unique failure signature.
The October 14 incident stopped during a CPU-only legacy trajectory after native GPU checks. A common cause across the incidents is unproven.
The latest shader and GPU host differ from the preceding successful full replay. Earlier passes cannot establish that the current optimization is safe.

comparison.reason: Host CPU exceeded 85 percent for two seconds

comparisonEvidence: Interrupted-run files are preserved alongside this file. Other IDs resolve under ../../development/<id>/supervisor/{report.json,telemetry.jsonl}; development/index.json records their hashes. Values above are rounded summaries, not new measurements.

confirmedHarnessWeaknesses.finding: Synchronous fsync/replace, output forwarding, filesystem stats and OS queries share the deadline loop. Blocking there prevents timely cancellation. This is a design limitation, not proof that a particular call hung.

Replay polling launches a CLI subprocess every 0.5 seconds plus call time and prints unchanged status. Any new stdout bytes reset the supervisor's stall timer; it does not measure verified simulation progress. The separate overall deadlines still exist.

Each tick performs full readback, unpacking, number-array conversion, canonical-byte allocation and hashing. At 64 cubed this is 3 MiB per state and at least 3 GiB readback over 1024 ticks, excluding extra copies. The explicit 5 ms yield occurs every 16 ticks. Peak job memory does not demonstrate a leak.
Detailed digests and durations remain in browser memory until completion. Durable records lack per-tick start and encode/submit/map/hash phases.
The 1500 ms timeout uses a browser-thread timer armed after submission/map calls. It cannot interrupt a blocked native call or guarantee recovery from a driver/kernel hang.

The outer source-bound receipt is written after the child exits. The interrupted stage has no durable start manifest; its source binding is inherited from the preceding tiny check and labeled accordingly.

recommendation: Keep recovery blocked. Review the proposed harness redesign in 3D_M5.md, then use a separate physical GPU test host for hardware reproduction and eventual full verification. Smaller local jobs reduce exposure but cannot establish safety on this workstation.
